content:
Quick note on how to handle results we upstream to Mathlib, now that the blueprint runs on LeanArchitect.

When one declaration lands in Mathlib, we shouldn't keep a local sorry copy of it. Once the Mathlib PR is merged and we've bumped to a Mathlib that includes it, we should just delete the local statement and re-tag the blueprint node directly onto the Mathlib declaration:

attribute [blueprint "thm:our-label" (statement := /-- ... -/)] Mathlib.Path.To.the_lemma

We should just reuse the original label so the node keeps its place in the dependency graph. LeanArchitect then sees the declaration lives in Mathlib and emits \mathlibok automatically, so the node turns dark green ("in Mathlib") in the dependency graph.

Of course this only works after the declaration is actually in our pinned Mathlib. Pointing attribute [blueprint] at a not-yet-merged PR is an "unknown identifier" build error, so while a Mathlib PR is still open the local placeholder has to stay. (Concretely: the IwaniecKowalskiCh1 lemmas commented #36495 aren't ready yet since that PR is still open, so they remain local for now, despite the "upstreamed" comments.)

I documented the workflow in LeanArchitect's README: https://github.com/hanwenzhu/LeanArchitect/pull/12.

I also opened (and merged) PNT#1460, which defines \mathlibok/\notready in the PDF preamble so the print build won't break the moment we start tagging upstreamed declarations (the web build already handles them nicely).
